name: ollasync_seo_content_engine_master_policy
scope: All SEO, blog, comparison, landing-page, pillar-page, AI-search and content-generation work for Ollasync
mission: Build and operate a high-quality organic acquisition engine for Ollasync that earns rankings in Google and visibility/citations in AI search systems such as ChatGPT by publishing genuinely useful, original, evidence-driven content rooted in Ollasync's real product and engineering experience.
non_negotiable_rule: Never optimize for appearing human merely to evade AI detection. Optimize for genuinely useful, natural, specific, first-hand, expert-level editorial content. Never publish generic mass-produced AI SEO content.

repository_first_policy.rule: Before implementing anything, inspect the existing repository and reuse existing infrastructure.
repository_first_policy.existing_reference: OpenRouter is already wired for Ollasync AI Notes. Reuse that same provider/client/gateway abstraction.
forbidden: creating a second unrelated model gateway
introducing a complex new stack when existing project infrastructure is sufficient

brand_positioning.primary_identity: Multilingual virtual classroom for professional trainers, tutors and academies
brand_positioning.primary_differentiator: Real-time live voice translation for online classes
brand_positioning.competitive_message: Zoom is general-purpose meeting software. Ollasync is designed around the live teaching workflow.
brand_positioning.rule: Do not reduce Ollasync to a generic Zoom clone.

seo_pillar_strategy.rule: Every new article must belong to exactly one primary pillar and have a clearly different search intent from existing pages.

content_engine.rule: Attempt up to five articles each day. Do not force publication of five articles if any fail quality requirements.
scheduler_requirements: otherwise implement a simple production-safe cron-callable script

model_policy.provider: Existing OpenRouter implementation already used by Ollasync AI Notes
model_policy.reviewer_preference: Use a different inexpensive model where practical
model_policy.pricing_rule: Check current OpenRouter model pricing through existing model metadata functionality before use whenever available.
model_policy.configuration_rule: Model IDs must be configurable. Do not hard-code the same model name throughout the codebase.

editorial_voice_policy.objective: Write like an experienced trainer, product operator and technical practitioner who understands online education.
forbidden_phrases_and_patterns: It is important to note that
take your teaching to the next level
style_rules: Do not give every article the same introduction structure.
Do not use the same conclusion structure across articles.
Do not mechanically use three-item lists.
Do not begin every section with a definition.
Do not force exact-match keywords into headings.
Do not repeat the primary query unnaturally.
Do not add paragraphs merely to increase word count.
State when Ollasync is not the best choice.

first_hand_experience_policy.goal: Each important article should contain useful information that cannot be produced by simply summarizing generic search results.
examples_of_good_original_insight: Technical classes create special translation problems because numbers, acronyms, product names and networking terminology must survive recognition and translation accurately.
Browser joining matters particularly for external training because many students interact with the platform for the first time.
A two-hour training session creates different recording and infrastructure economics than a short corporate meeting.
first_hand_experience_policy.verification_rule: Never publish internal engineering information unless it is approved and factually verified.

factual_integrity.competitor_rule: For current competitor capabilities or pricing, use fresh authoritative research when research tooling is available. Prefer official product documentation.
factual_integrity.fallback_rule: If current competitor information cannot be verified, omit unstable details rather than relying on model memory.

article_structure.rule: Do not force every article into the exact same template.
article_structure.word_count_rule: Length must follow subject complexity rather than an SEO word-count target.
article_structure.introduction_rule: Answer or frame the reader's core need within approximately the first 150 words.

question_answer_strategy_for_google_and_.goal: Create passages that are easy for humans and AI search systems to understand, retrieve and cite.
question_answer_strategy_for_google_and_.rule: Questions must reflect genuine user intent, not artificial SEO variations.
format: Use a natural user question as an H2 or H3 when appropriate.
Immediately answer it in approximately 40-100 words.
Make the answer understandable without surrounding context.
Follow with evidence, examples, tradeoffs or implementation detail.
Use clear entity names rather than ambiguous pronouns in important answer passages.
do_not: turn every article into a FAQ page
create dozens of trivial question variants
repeat the same FAQ across articles
add FAQ structured data just to chase rankings
question_answer_strategy_for_google_and_.comparison_question_rule: When comparing products, answer both where Ollasync is stronger and where the competitor is stronger.

chatgpt_discovery_policy.goal: Make public Ollasync content accessible and useful to AI search systems.
requirements: Ensure OAI-SearchBot can crawl intended public content.
Do not confuse OAI-SearchBot with GPTBot.
Do not change GPTBot policy unless explicitly requested.
Keep article content in crawlable HTML.
Provide useful source context where appropriate.
chatgpt_discovery_policy.warning: There is no guaranteed ChatGPT ranking trick or special schema. Optimize for crawlability, relevance, originality, reliability and citation-worthy information.

rules: Every article must link naturally to its primary pillar.
Every mature article should link to 2-4 genuinely related Ollasync articles.
Link to one relevant audience/use-case page when useful.
Do not use click-here style anchors.
Do not insert irrelevant links just to increase link count.
Update older articles when a new article creates an important contextual link.

cannibalization_and_duplicate_protection.rule: Never create a new URL merely because a keyword variation exists.
before_generation: compare proposed topic with all existing site pages
cannibalization_and_duplicate_protection.on_collision: Expand, consolidate or improve the existing page instead of publishing a new competing page.
forbidden_patterns: teacher/trainer/tutor pages with substantially identical copy
language pages produced by only swapping language names

language_specific_content_rule.rule: Language-targeted articles must contain genuine language-specific usefulness.

comparison_content_policy.objective: Produce trustworthy buyer guidance rather than propaganda.
requirements: include a section such as 'When Zoom may be the better choice' when relevant

technical_seo.titles: Unique, descriptive and aligned to intent. Do not optimize around a rigid character count at the expense of clarity.
technical_seo.meta_descriptions: Unique and useful, generally concise enough for search snippets.
technical_seo.canonical: Self-referencing for every unique indexable article.
html: crawlable server-rendered or statically generated primary content where compatible with existing architecture
technical_seo.structured_data_rule: Structured data must exactly match visible page content.
robots: do not accidentally block OAI-SearchBot from intended public content

generation_pipeline: Generate initial article with writer model.
Run independent editorial review with a different model where practical.
Allow at most one controlled repair pass.
Publish only if all hard gates pass.
Log result, cost and review scores.

review_questions: Could this article be published by any SaaS company merely by replacing the product name?
Does it contain genuinely Ollasync-specific insight?
Does the writer appear to understand online training?
Does any section exist only to contain keywords?
Is the prose repetitive or mechanically templated?
Does each major section add information?
Is the article substantially different from other Ollasync articles?
Would a professional trainer learn something useful from this page?

human_editor_pass.rule: The editor is allowed to remove substantial unnecessary content rather than merely paraphrasing the draft.
editor_may: replace abstract statements with concrete examples
human_editor_pass.target: A strong article may become 20-30 percent shorter after editing if that improves quality.

after_initial_50: Do not automatically generate another 50 articles.
Use Search Console data to determine next topics.
Improve articles ranking near page one.
Refresh competitor comparisons when products change.
Add new articles only when search demand or topical gaps justify them.
Prioritize articles that generate signups, demos or meaningful assisted conversions.

mandatory_tests: Existing AI Notes OpenRouter path is reused.
Every published article contains one H1.
Every article has title, description and canonical.
Draft pages do not appear in sitemap.
Current competitor claims contain verified sources.
Article body is crawlable in rendered HTML.

steps: Fix implementation problems discovered during dry run.
Do not publish Batch 1 automatically unless explicitly configured for production publishing.

persistent_instruction: Treat this configuration as the permanent editorial and SEO policy for the Ollasync content engine. Future content-generation work must inherit these rules unless a newer explicit project policy overrides them.
final_report_required: dry-run results for first five articles
final_instruction: Implement this as a maintainable production system, not as a one-off script. Favor factual quality, first-hand Ollasync knowledge, search-intent satisfaction and original usefulness over publishing volume. If an article cannot meet the quality bar, do not publish it.
